description: PF07 - the page-up key - pressed on page THREE, which is the only state in which the dispatcher reaches 9100-READ-BACKWARDS: the browse walks BACKWARDS from the top of page three to redisplay page two, and the page number is decremented rather than left alone. This is the sibling of case06, where PF07 arrives on page one, the WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK07 AND CA-FIRST-PAGE arm at :444-445 wins instead, the same page is re-read FORWARD and the page number is untouched. PROVENANCE (practice B12): every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED from app/cbl/COCRDLIC.cbl [:177-178, :229-248, :311, :327-331, :336-343, :370-380, :410-414, :501-511, :604-619, :643-671, :678-743, :837-889, :897-923, :924, :926-930, :1268, :1273, :1284-1286, :1287-1288, :1294, :1307, :1322, :1339-1347, :1351-1353, :1375], the byte layouts of app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy and app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, the symbolic-map definitions of app/cpy-bms/COCRDLI.CPY with app/bms/COCRDLI.bms, and the real fixture app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - and NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution, which the eight verified blockers of AAP 0.7.6 make impossible in this environment (risk R-A, AAP 0.9.11). No user rules exist for this project - review_rules returns exactly the one line 'No user rules provided.', and that one line is the whole document - so AAP 0.10.2's enterprise practices govern instead. Encoding is US-ASCII, named explicitly and never the platform default (practice B8), and the clock is pinned to the same 2022-07-19T23:12:34 as case01 so CURDATEO renders 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO 23:12:34 on every run (practice B7). ENTRY STATE: EIBCALEN is greater than zero and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-THISPGM, so :357-362 performs 2000-RECEIVE-MAP, and the re-init guard at :336-337 stays false for the same reason - the from-program is this program, so INITIALIZE WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA does not run and the paging cursor survives the round trip. eibcalen is stated as LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, 160, in line with COCRDLIC's other re-entry cases; recorded rather than corrected (practice B4), the value CICS would actually report is 2000, because COMMON-RETURN returns COMMAREA(WS-COMMAREA) LENGTH(LENGTH OF WS-COMMAREA) at :615-618 over WS-COMMAREA PIC X(2000), of which only the leading 414 bytes are meaningful - CARDDEMO-COMMAREA 160 plus WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA 254. Nothing behavioural rests on the number: :315, :357 and :839 test it only against zero. CURSOR: the paging cursor travels in the payload and nowhere else (rule R6, gate G37), and it arrives here on the third page - WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM 3, so 88 CA-FIRST-PAGE VALUE 1 at :238 is FALSE and :502's NOT CA-FIRST-PAGE is satisfied without any server-side state being consulted. It is declared among the commarea items because that is what the inbound DFHCOMMAREA physically is: :327-331 restores CARDDEMO-COMMAREA from bytes 1 to 160 and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA from bytes 161 to 414 of one area, so the WS-CA-... items are as much part of the communication area as the CDEMO-... ones. COTRN00C does the same thing with the extension it happens to name CDEMO-CT00-... [COTRN00C.cbl:62-70]. The cursor states the page three the operator is on: WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY is fixture row 15, which :1174-1176 stored when page three was painted, WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY is fixture row 22, which the look-ahead READNEXT at :1197 found and :1212-1214 substituted, WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED is 9 per 88 CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN at :241, WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND is 'Y' per 88 CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS at :244, and WS-RETURN-FLAG is the space that INITIALIZE left in it - the field is declared at :246-248 and never assigned anywhere in the program, so its 88 WS-RETURN-FLAG-ON is dead and it is carried unchanged (practice B5). AID: DFHPF7 resolves through app/cpy/CSSTRPFY.cpy [:42-43], copied at :1416, to SET CCARD-AID-PFK07. PF07 is one of the four keys :371-374 accepts, so :370's PFK-INVALID is overturned at :375 and :378-380 does not coerce anything to ENTER. Because the key is not PF08, :410-414 re-asserts CA-LAST-PAGE-NOT-SHOWN, which was already 9. THE DISPATCHER ARM (gate G30, rule R7): the :418-583 EVALUATE TRUE is ordered and every arm ahead of the page-up arm is refused in turn - WHEN INPUT-ERROR at :419 because both filters arrive blank and no selection character was typed; the duplicated WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK07 AND CA-FIRST-PAGE pair at :439-440 and :444-445 because the page number is 3 and not 1; WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK03 at :458 because the key is PF07; WHEN CDEMO-PGM-REENTER AND CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM NOT EQUAL LIT-THISPGM at :459-460 because the from-program IS this program; and WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK08 AND CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS at :486-487 because the key is not PF08. So WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK07 AND NOT CA-FIRST-PAGE at :501-502 is the arm that runs, and reversing any of that order would change the answer. Its body is: MOVE WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-NUM TO WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM [:504-505], SUBTRACT 1 FROM WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM [:508], PERFORM 9100-READ-BACKWARDS THRU 9100-READ-BACKWARDS-EXIT [:509-510], PERFORM 1000-SEND-MAP THRU 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT [:511-512] - the FULL range, where the PF07-on-page-one arm at :452-453 writes THRU 1000-SEND-MAP - and GO TO COMMON-RETURN [:513], a benign shared-terminal jump restructured to a return after the shared finalisation at :604-619 with the fall-through outcome unchanged. Beside it sits the commented-out MOVE WS-CA-FIRST-CARD-ACCT-ID TO WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID at :506-507, whose live twin at :504-505 moves only the card number: dead code, preserved as a no-op, so the browse is keyed on the sixteen-byte card number alone (practices B4 and B5). THE NAMED COMPUTE, which is why this case exists (gate G28): 9100-READ-BACKWARDS is the only paragraph in COCRDLIC that computes its row counter rather than accumulating it. :1266 blanks WS-ALL-ROWS; :1268 MOVE WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY TO WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY copies the page's first key into its last key BEFORE the browse begins, which is why the outbound last key is page three's first record and not anything the browse read (practice B5); :1273-1280 STARTBR ... GTEQ anchors at or after fixture row 15; and then COMPUTE WS-SCRN-COUNTER = WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES + 1 at :1284-1286 primes the counter to EIGHT, because WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES is PIC S9(4) COMP VALUE 7 at :177-178. :1287 sets CA-NEXT-PAGE-EXISTS and :1288 sets MORE-RECORDS-TO-READ before a single record has been read. The READPREV at :1294 then returns the record at the anchor - fixture row 15, the one already at the top of the current page - and its arm at :1305-1307 DISCARDS it: SUBTRACT 1 FROM WS-SCRN-COUNTER and nothing else, leaving the counter at SEVEN. The loop at :1320-1371 reads backwards with the READPREV at :1322 and, for each record the filter keeps, writes WS-ROW-CARD-NUM, WS-ROW-ACCTNO and WS-ROW-CARD-STATUS at subscript WS-SCRN-COUNTER [:1338-1344] and only THEN decrements [:1346], stopping when the counter reaches 0 [:1347]. That places fixture row 14 in screen row 7, row 13 in row 6, row 12 in row 5, row 11 in row 4, row 10 in row 3, row 9 in row 2 and row 8 in screen row 1: seven placements, counter 7 down to 0, a DESCENDING fill that is the exact inverse of 9000-READ-FORWARD's ADD 1 TO WS-SCRN-COUNTER at :1163 and its ascending fill. The page still READS ascending by card number, because a KSDS browse walked backwards and stored backwards comes out in key order. The record that filled screen row 1 - fixture row 8 - becomes the new WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY at :1350-1353. There is no look-ahead read and no ENDFILE arm in this paragraph, so the whole of the eight-priming, the two SUBTRACT sites and the = 0 terminator is load-bearing, and so is the SUBTRACT 1 FROM WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM at :508 that makes PAGENOO 2. BROWSE (gate G47): this is the only case in the twenty that drives the BACKWARD call sites - STARTBR at :1273, the discarded READPREV at :1294, the loop READPREV at :1322 and the ENDBR at :1375 - and every one of them reports the NORMAL outcome, DFHRESP(NORMAL), which is common/FileStatus.NORMAL and its Outcome.OK. Nothing is forced: the eight records the browse reads all exist in the seed, so no arm is reached that a forced failure would be needed for. 9500-FILTER-RECORDS excludes nothing because both filter flags arrive blank [:1385, :1396]. The ENDBR lives in 9100-READ-BACKWARDS-EXIT at :1375-1377 rather than in the paragraph body, which is what lets the GO TO 9100-READ-BACKWARDS-EXIT at :1317 reach it too - a benign forward early exit, restructured to a return with the fall-through outcome unchanged (rule R7). THE MESSAGE, and the assertion it is easiest to get wrong (gate G30): 1400-SETUP-MESSAGE's EVALUATE at :897-922 is ordered, and arm three - WHEN CCARD-AID-PFK07 AND CA-FIRST-PAGE at :901-904, the one that moves 'NO PREVIOUS PAGES TO DISPLAY' into WS-ERROR-MSG - does NOT match here, because :508 has already made WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM 2. That message must therefore be absent from this screen, which is exactly what separates this case from case06. Arms one and two [:898-900] do not match either, since neither filter was supplied, and the two PF08 arms [:905-916] cannot match a PF07. Arm six, WHEN WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE at :917, DOES match: 1100-SCREEN-INIT has just executed SET WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE TO TRUE at :669, and 88 WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE VALUES SPACES LOW-VALUES at :113-114 is satisfied by the spaces it left. Arm six carries no statements of its own, so under COBOL multi-WHEN semantics it shares arm seven's body and SET WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS TO TRUE runs [:919]. Consequently the guard at :926-927 is TRUE - the info message is no longer the no-message state and WS-NO-RECORDS-FOUND was never set, since that only happens on the forward path at :1244 - so :928-929 move WS-INFO-MSG into INFOMSGO and DFHNEUTR into INFOMSGC, replacing the DFHBMDAR of :671. INFOMSGO is therefore the 41-character literal of 88 WS-INFORM-REC-ACTIONS at :115-116 padded to the 45 bytes of INFOMSGI PIC X(45), and ERRMSGO is what :924 moves: WS-ERROR-MSG is still the SPACES that SET WS-ERROR-MSG-OFF gave it at :311 [88 at :118], moved from PIC X(75) into ERRMSGO PIC X(78), so it is 75 spaces right-padded with 3 more to 78. SCREEN: :643 MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCRDLIAO paints the output group x'00' and not spaces, which is why ACCTSIDO, CARDSIDO, CRDSEL1O through CRDSEL7O and CRDSTP2O through CRDSTP7O are all expected as LOW-VALUES rather than blanks - the distinction is behaviour and not taste, since 88 SELECT-BLANK VALUES ' ', LOW-VALUES at :80-82 and IF WS-EACH-CARD(n) EQUAL LOW-VALUES at :680 both test for it. The six CRDSTPnO stopper items are never written by 1200-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT at all: it moves exactly four items per row [:683-686 and its six repeats], and row one has no stopper field to move [COCRDLI.CPY:78-96], so they are preserved as :643 left them (practice B5). Each CRDSELnO carries LOW-VALUES because 2100-RECEIVE-SCREEN moves the untransmitted CRDSELnI items into WS-EDIT-SELECT at :972-978 and 1200-SCREEN-ARRAY-INIT moves them back out at :683 onward; a 3270 transmits only modified fields, and pressing PF07 modifies none. TITLE01O and TITLE02O are the byte-exact literals of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, TITLE02O taking the ACTIVE line 22 and not the commented-out line 21. PAGENOO is '2  ' and not '002' or '  2': MOVE WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM TO PAGENOO OF CCRDLIAO at :667 sends a PIC 9(1) into a PIC X(3), and an alphanumeric receiver left-justifies and pads on the right. Because this is a re-entry, 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS takes the ELSE at :843, and its two ordered EVALUATEs land on WHEN CDEMO-ACCT-ID = 0 at :849-850 and WHEN CDEMO-CARD-NUM = 0 at :861-862, because the blank-filter branches of 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT and 2220-EDIT-CARD zeroed both, so ACCTSIDO and CARDSIDO are LOW-VALUES. The cursor request is ACCTSIDL, from IF INPUT-OK MOVE -1 TO ACCTSIDL at :884-885. NO HIGHLIGHT (gate G38): 2000-RECEIVE-MAP does run, but there is no input error to redden. The blank filters take the not-supplied branches at :1007-1012 and :1042-1047, 2250-EDIT-ARRAY tallies zero actions and finds every row SELECT-BLANK, INPUT-ERROR is never set, and so neither 1250-SETUP-ARRAY-ATTRIBS' DFHRED nor the '*' of the CSSETATY pattern appears - COCRDLIC does not copy CSSETATY and drives its own per-row flags instead. The only attribute item carrying a value is INFOMSGC. OUTBOUND CURSOR: the 58-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA prefix [:229-248] leaves with WS-CA-FIRST-CARDKEY taken from fixture row 8 (1561409106491600 with account 00000000035) by :1350-1353, WS-CA-LAST-CARDKEY still holding fixture row 15 (3766281984155154 with account 00000000041) because :1268 copied it there before the browse and 9100-READ-BACKWARDS never writes that field again, WS-CA-SCREEN-NUM 2 after the SUBTRACT at :508, WS-CA-LAST-PAGE-DISPLAYED 9, WS-CA-NEXT-PAGE-IND 'Y' from :1287 and WS-RETURN-FLAG unchanged. It is documented here rather than pinned because the compared fingerprint carries the next program, mapset and map, the communication area, the sends, the cursor item and the termination - the paging cursor reaches the client in the response payload and is asserted by this suite's targeted tests. PAGE SIZE: seven rows, from WS-MAX-SCREEN-LINES PIC S9(4) COMP VALUE 7 at :177-178, and here the 7 is an arithmetic OPERAND - the 8 that :1284-1286 primes the counter to is literally 7 + 1 - which makes it doubly behaviour rather than configuration. This case therefore declares no page-size parameter of any kind (gate G39), and no jobParameters at all, because a CONTROLLER_POJO takes none. RECORDS: CARDDAT is the single dataset key this program reaches (gate G45); CARDAIX, declared at :215-217 as LIT-CARD-FILE-ACCT-PATH, is never opened by COCRDLIC and stays declared-but-unused. All fifty seeded rows are pinned unchanged, which is a positive assertion rather than an omission: a browse-and-return transaction must leave the card master exactly as it found it, and a backward browse must leave it no differently than a forward one. Each image is 150 bytes summed by hand from app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy - CARD-NUM 16, CARD-ACCT-ID 11, CARD-CVV-CD 3, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME 50, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE 10, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS 1, FILLER 59 (practice B11, gates G19 and G21). Rows 7, 13 and 14 zero-based - the record that fills screen row 1 and becomes the new first key, the record the loop places FIRST into screen row 7, and the browse anchor whose record the READPREV at :1294 discards - are additionally pinned span by span, so the misspelled CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE at offsets 81 to 90 is asserted BY NAME exactly as the copybook spells it (requirement I1) and the FILLER at 92 to 150 is asserted as 59 spaces rather than merely implied by the total width. NOT APPLICABLE HERE, stated so its absence is deliberate: gates G32 and G35 have no subject in this program, and the backward browse must not be mistaken for either. READPREV is a data-access DIRECTION, not a backward GO TO: all 16 of COCRDLIC's GO TO sites are forward early exits or the shared terminal COMMON-RETURN, there is no loop-forming backward jump anywhere in it - CBSTM03A is the only program that has one - and RETURN-CODE, CEE3ABD and ABEND occur exactly zero times in the source, so a completed transaction reports 0 and expectedReturnCode says so. None of the three XCTL sites at :402, :538 and :566 is reached on this path, so nextProgram, nextMapset and nextMap are absent and the termination is RETURN_TRANSID with exactly one send. One further discrepancy is recorded rather than fixed (practice B4): app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy declares SIXTEEN 88-level conditions over CCARD-AID PIC X(5) - ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2 and PFK01 through PFK12 - where AAP 0.3.3 says fifteen. The copybook is the contract; the count in the prose is left alone. GATE: this is one of the twenty cases COCRDLIC must satisfy, and the module is not complete until the diff count is zero across all twenty of them (gates G15 and G18). The unit is reached as a plain object with no HTTP in the path (gate G51).
